title: The Battle of Tours
description: October 732. Charles Martel's Frankish infantry must hold the wooded high ground between Tours and Poitiers against the Umayyad cavalry of Abd al-Rahman. A third force of Aquitanian allies under Duke Odo can be rallied to strike the enemy camp. Victory requires repelling the cavalry charges and forcing the invaders' withdrawal.

anachronisms_found: Player One's leader is WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR, a mounted Norman hero of 1066, standing in for Charles Martel — and mounted, which contradicts the scenario's own 'shield wall' of dismounted Frankish infantry
Player Two's leader is SALADIN (d. 1193, Ayyubid Egypt/Syria) representing the Umayyad emir Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi of 732 — over four centuries and a different dynasty removed

Player Three's leader is EL_CID (Castilian, d. 1099) representing Duke Odo of Aquitaine — wrong century and wrong polity, and an odd choice given El Cid fought Muslim and Christian rulers in Iberia, not Umayyad invaders in Gaul

KNIGHT units in the Umayyad roster: heavy Western-style lancers for an Arab-Berber raiding army; the engine offers Camel Rider, Light Cavalry and Cavalry Archer, which are used elsewhere in the roster, so the Knights were avoidable
PIKEMAN (a 14th-century weapon system) among the Frankish line where SPEARMAN/MILITIA/MAN_AT_ARMS would have sufficed

A full economic/military base for the Franks (TOWN_CENTER, BLACKSMITH, MONASTERY, ARCHERY_RANGE, two GUARD_TOWERS) on what the text describes as an improvised wooded ridge position — the Franks fought from a field formation, not a fortified settlement

issues_found: Charles Martel is represented by the WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR hero — a Norman duke of 1066, three centuries later and a different polity; a renamed generic Frankish champion/paladin would have been the correct substitution.

Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi is represented by SALADIN, a 12th-century Kurdish Ayyubid sultan — wrong dynasty, wrong culture, wrong century by over 450 years, and the victory trigger is literally keyed on DESTROY_OBJECT of SALADIN.
Duke Odo of Aquitaine is represented by EL_CID, an 11th-century Castilian — wrong realm and era; a renamed generic knight would have been better.

Both active players are set to civilization RANDOM, so architecture and unit bonuses are unassigned; Franks (and a Saracen/Berber-flavoured civ for the Umayyads) were available and would have fixed the building set.

Player 3 (Odo) is given SCOUT_CAVALRY and KNIGHT with no infantry at all; the Aquitanian contingent that raided the camp was a mixed force, and the tiny 20-unit armies understate a battle of tens of thousands even allowing for scale abstraction.
Umayyad roster leans on CAMEL_RIDER x7; the Andalusian host at Tours was overwhelmingly horse, and the engine's light/heavy cavalry would have been closer.

Charles Martel is represented by the WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR hero — a Norman duke of 1066, over three centuries after Tours; a renamed generic Frankish champion/paladin was available and would have been correct.
Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi is represented by SALADIN, a 12th-century Ayyubid sultan of an entirely different dynasty and era; again avoidable via a renamed Saracen cavalry unit.
Duke Odo of Aquitaine is represented by EL_CID, an 11th-century Castilian — wrong culture, wrong polity, wrong century.
Both active players are set to civilization RANDOM, so architecture, unit skins and bonuses are undefined; Franks vs Saracens were obvious and available assignments.

Player 2's Umayyad force includes 6 KNIGHTS (Frankish/European heavy cavalry look) alongside camels and cavalry archers, blurring the visual distinction between the two armies — Saracen mamluks/light cavalry would have read better.
Frankish force is tiny (20 infantry) against a similarly tiny mounted force; the sources describe a large Frankish infantry mass, and 4,758 objects are almost entirely trees rather than troops.
Player 2 holds a lone VILLAGER_MALE and only tents/pavilions for the 'camp' that Odo is supposed to burn — the plunder-laden Umayyad baggage camp central to the narrative is barely represented.
